recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中多顆紅血球母細胞的胞質（及其上方）布滿粗大深藍色點狀顆粒，中央一顆細胞淡染胞質內有散在粗顆粒，呈現粗大嗜鹼性點彩（basophilic stippling）。
features: Increased erythroid precursors at various stages
Coarse dark blue punctate stippling in the cytoplasm of many erythroblasts
Central cell with dense dark nucleus and pale cytoplasm containing discrete coarse dark granules
Some red cells and a nucleated red cell with small inclusions
Occasional granulocytes and a band neutrophil at left
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows numerous erythroid precursors, many of which contain coarse, dark blue punctate cytoplasmic stippling. A central cell with a dense nucleus shows discrete coarse dark granules scattered in pale cytoplasm; a basophil is a morphologic consideration for that cell, although the pattern matches the adjacent stippled erythroblasts. A few mature red cells contain small inclusions. Findings are suggestive of coarse basophilic stippling of erythroid precursors, as seen in pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase deficiency, lead poisoning, or dyserythropoiesis; an iron stain is recommended to exclude siderotic granules.

ddx.vs: Siderotic granules are fewer, clustered at one pole, and stain positively with Prussian blue, whereas basophilic stippling is diffuse and iron-negative.
Basophil granules are larger, purple-black, water-soluble, and overlie a lobulated nucleus in a mature granulocyte rather than an erythroblast.
Precipitate is present over the background and in varying focal planes, not confined to cytoplasm.
